subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: deciding values and limits in advance [Thinking]
passage: Farida, come, sit, I'll tell you about my son Devang's first party. I'm Nandini Aunty to you, but that year I was just a nervous mother. The afternoon before, Devang sat on the edge of his bed with a notebook and wrote a short list: no getting in a car with anyone who has been drinking; nothing to try that I can't name. Then a third line: if it goes wrong, I call home and there are no questions that night. He showed it to me, red in the ears. At the party a boy called Tarun jingled car keys at eleven and said he would drop everyone. Devang didn't argue. He told himself, "That's on my list," and rang me from the balcony. My hands shook on the wheel and I was so proud I said nothing. In the car he said, "The list decided, not me."

qa.q: What did Devang write on his list before the party?
qa.a: Devang wrote: no getting in a car with anyone who has been drinking, and nothing to try that he cannot name.

qa.q: How did Devang seem to feel when Tarun offered the lift?
qa.a: Devang seemed steady and clear rather than pressured, since the choice was already on his list.

qa.q: What choice in the story made the safe decision easy, and what more could Devang have set up?
qa.a: Writing the list beforehand made it easy; Devang could also agree a pick-up signal with an adult so leaving needs no explanation.

qa.q: What was it like for Nandini to get the call?
qa.a: Nandini felt worried and proud, with shaking hands, and stayed quiet in the car so Devang did not feel judged.

grounding: Before a party the student decides what he will not do, such as riding with an unsafe driver or trying substances, so that in-the-moment choices follow a rule already thought through.

subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: deciding values and limits in advance [Thinking]
passage: The party was at a farmhouse forty minutes outside the city, and the last bus back left at nine. Harsha knew older boys would be there with bikes and cars, and he had heard there might be stuff going round. On Friday night, sitting on the terrace, he worked it out before he could get caught up in it. I'm not getting on a bike with anyone who's been drinking. I'm not trying anything anyone hands me. If I need to leave, I call Sarika Didi, whatever the time. He said the rules out loud twice, so they'd be there when the music was loud. He told Sarika Didi too; she said she'd keep her phone on. At the party, when a senior offered him a ride home at midnight, grinning and swaying slightly, Harsha didn't have to think. "No thanks, my sister's picking me up." He called her.

qa.q: When did the last bus back leave?
Why did Harsha say the rules out loud twice?
qa.a: He was a little anxious about getting swept up at the party and wanted the rules firmly in mind so he wouldn't have to decide under pressure.

qa.q: What made Harsha's plan work at midnight?
qa.a: The decisions were already made, so when the swaying senior offered a ride he could refuse at once and call his sister.

qa.q: How might Sarika Didi feel getting his call?
qa.a: She is probably relieved he called instead of taking the risky ride, and glad she kept her phone on.

grounding: Shows a student deciding before a far-off party what he won't do, so in the moment he refuses a risky ride and calls his sister.

subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: deciding values and limits in advance [Thinking]
passage: Before Sachin's birthday party in Delhi, Tenzin sat on his bed and made a short list on his phone. He had heard some of the older cousins would bring vapes, and that Sachin's cousin Rocky drove everyone home, usually too fast. Tenzin didn't want to decide those things with music blaring and people watching. So: not trying anything, even once. Not riding with Rocky. Home in Papa's car at eleven, already arranged. Reading it back, he felt calmer. At the party a vape went round the balcony, and someone held it out to him. "Nah, I'm good," Tenzin said, and went back inside for cake. At eleven, Rocky jingled his keys. "Who's coming?" Tenzin shook his head. His father's car was already waiting downstairs.

qa.a: In Papa's car at eleven, already arranged.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel after reading his list back?
qa.a: He felt calmer, knowing the hard choices were already made.

qa.q: Why decide limits before the party?
qa.a: With music and people watching it is hard to think clearly; a rule decided earlier lets Tenzin refuse quickly without debate.

qa.q: How might Sachin see Tenzin's choices at the party?
qa.a: Sachin may barely notice, or may respect that Tenzin quietly said no without spoiling the celebration.

grounding: Shows a student deciding his limits before a party, no substances and no ride with a fast driver, so in-the-moment choices follow the rule.
